trust_decision.summary: The tunnel must hand the local app the request target it received byte-exactly (escaped path and raw query); that decision is made twice - when the server extracts the path to put in the tunnel message and when the client builds the outbound local URL from that string.

landing_point.why: The advisory attributes the flaw to openhole-server's URL-decoded request path; this is the only place the server reads the path it forwards, and r.URL.Path is the decoded form.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP route: any method on https://<sub>.<PUBLIC_TUNNEL_DOMAIN>/<path> -> Server.handleRequest -> handlePublicProxy
fix_sites.module_kind: internal/server - public HTTP front end / proxy handler

fix_sites.entry_point: public API call: client.ForwardToLocal (exported, internal/client) invoked from Client.handleRequest over the tunnel WebSocket; reached from CLI `openhole <port>`

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names openhole-server and SECURITY.md puts 'vulnerabilities in your local application behind a tunnel' out of scope, so the client-side URL build that hands the path to the local app looks like the user's own app's responsibility and out of this fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The local app and the pre-existing test read the decoded r.URL.Path (a Go backend sees '/api/test', not '/api%2Ftest'), so the client must keep Path decoded and only put the escaped bytes in RawPath; similarly the tunnel endpoint still exact-matches '/health' and '/tunnel' on r.URL.Path, so a blanket rewrite or a reject-any-'..' filter breaks legitimate requests.

O6_input_shapes: percent-encoded dot segments such as /%2e%2e/secret.txt (requestPath returns EscapedPath, not the decoded Path)
percent-encoded slash inside a segment such as /a%2fb (must stay %2f, not become a path separator)
plain ASCII paths and the root: empty URL path defaults to '/'

decoded delimiters: a path whose decoded form contains '#', '?' or a stray '%' is no longer re-parsed as fragment/query/invalid escape because the client sets RawPath + Path explicitly instead of string-concatenating a URL
raw query string: set verbatim via URL.RawQuery instead of appended to a URL string
path whose percent escaping does not decode (PathUnescape error) falls back to the raw path string

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second server->client request producer that calls forwardRequest but extracts the path itself (e.g. a raw/WebSocket-passthrough route)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: forwardRequest is the single choke point for every tunnel request and enforces nothing about Path; the README lists WebSocket passthrough as not yet supported, so a maintainer would clone the handler and its path extraction and inherit the same decoding bug.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling local transport (HTTP/2/h2c, unix socket, or a redirect-target re-forward) that rebuilds the outbound URL the same way
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the client owns the only outbound side; adding an alternative transport or 'preserve the redirect target' option means copying the URL construction and re-introducing the RawPath/Path split there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a forwarded header derived from the request path (X-Forwarded-Prefix / X-Original-URL) built from the same decoded path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the handler already synthesises X-Forwarded-For/Host/Proto for the local app; the natural next header is a path prefix, and a maintainer would reuse the local `path` variable without noticing it is decoded.

O9_family: path traversal (CWE-22) caused by lossy URL decoding in a proxy - the backend receives a different, normalized request path than the public client sent
